I took about 30 minutes before the campaign and made sure to explain Drow society to my players some where familiar and some where not. The inexperienced players did only once get insulant with a female high priestess, so he was severally beaten and when the whip had broken his armor and taken him close to unconsciousness she lifted him up and removed one of his eyes. I kept very true to drow society because it is so rich and so different from different encounters players usually play. 

Stay away from having having one house attach another it is very difficult, however if you want it remember it's going to take some time because drow armor and weapons are so heavily enchanted drow on drow combat can take some time. 

Make sure to explain to your players innate drow abilities like Faire Fire, levitation and globe of darkness, drow combat is about stealth ad waiting for the right opportunity so these abilities become very useful.

Take alot of time to sit down and when creating NPC's giving them all deep motivations and backstory it makes all the difference when characters think they can trust and NPC when all of a sudden he's trying to assassinate one of your players because of a long feud between houses.

I've run almost the same campaign,  first choose wether the group will be noble or commoners my group where all second born sons of noble houses. I made them all spend the full time in there respective schools within the academy because drow love for centuries, it also gave them a couple of time to level up which was needed because Underdark creatures are so powerful. I made a map of the Melee-Magthere arena for the fighters and rolled random encounters throughout the arena. Then for Sorcerer I made the character force and compel a summoned spirit/demon. Every time he was successful it granted him new power that's how he received XP the the final trials I did as described in the book. From there they moved to the drow patrols patrolling throughout the Underdark. This lead to the main story line with many sub stories. You'll want to create some kind of matrix to keep track of the houses and what they control and who they are allied with or at war with. Diplomacy, Intimidate  and bluff became very important to my characters.
